evals.prompt: Turn /Users/pawel.dworzycki/dev/backstage/AGENTS.md into an interactive adventure book in HTML. Theme: a medieval knight on a journey through the realm. I want fancy graphics and pop-outs that explain what each part of the story actually means in the real doc. Save it as agents-quest.html
evals.expected_output: A single self-contained HTML file that walks through AGENTS.md as a knight's quest: multiple navigable stages with illustrated SVG scenes, clickable pop-outs whose explanations quote the real commands/rules from AGENTS.md, and coverage of the major sections (setup, commands, architecture, testing, code style, rules).
expectations: A single .html output file exists in the outputs directory
Works offline: no external scripts, stylesheets, fonts or images are loaded
Contains substantial inline SVG illustration (several scenes, dozens of shapes), not just icons
Has click-to-reveal pop-outs (dialog/modal/details/tooltip) that hide explanatory text until activated
Page renders in headless Chrome with real content (JS ran, >300 words of rendered text)
Has at least 5 distinct navigable stages/chapters (not one long scroll)
Pop-out text names the real thing behind the allegory (e.g. 'VPN', 'PostgreSQL', a command) in plain language, not more story
The narrative reads as a themed story in second person with a consistent allegory, not a summary with costume words
The stages follow the source document's order so a reader could act on it afterwards
Concise: each stage's narrative is roughly 60-120 words, two short paragraphs at most, with no padded mood-setting or sentences that restate the previous one in themed words
Has a clear beginning, middle and end with a stated objective: the opening names what the hero must be able to do by the end, and the ending pays that objective off rather than just stopping
Stages are causally connected — each follows from the last ('therefore'/'but', not 'and then') and the middle escalates, so it reads as one journey rather than a list of themed vignettes
Legible without clicking: the sentence around each marked phrase carries the real meaning, so a reader who never opens a pop-out still understands what happens and why
Something goes wrong before the end (a real mistake, footgun or failure taken from the source), and the story shows the fix
Quotes the real setup and dev commands verbatim (yarn dev, bnw_login, docker compose up -d, yarn tsc)
Explains the plugin naming conventions with the real suffixes (@internal/, -backend, -backend-module-, -common)
Covers the major AGENTS.md sections: setup, commands, architecture, testing, code style, rules (at least 5 of 6 signal terms)
Carries the testing conventions: BDD/tests-first and no 'should' in test names
